name: Western Union
description: Western Union is a regulated cross-border money-transfer network for consumers, businesses, and approved partners. Customers use its web, mobile, and agent-location services to send and receive money through bank accounts, wallets, cards, and cash pickup where available.
agentUseSummary: Western Union is visible as a partner-review preview only. Relay will not collect a Western Union password, browser session, MTCN, access token, payment credential, or identity-verification data, and no agent action is callable until Western Union approves a supported partner API contract and authorization lifecycle for Relay.

capabilities.label: Read approved partner data
capabilities.description: After partner approval, expose only the provider-approved non-mutating corridor, quote, and exact transfer-status surface documented in Relay's signed partner contract.

blocked.label: Connect before partner approval
blocked.description: Relay has no current Western Union partner contract, approved application, production credentials, sandbox tenant, authorization lifecycle, permitted operation list, or compliance allocation.

blocked.label: Collect customer credentials
blocked.description: Relay will not ask customers for a Western Union password, browser session, bearer token, MTCN, payment credential, identity document, tax identifier, or verification response as a substitute for provider-approved authorization.

blocked.label: Run Western Union API actions
blocked.description: No corridor, quote, recipient, transfer, payment, payout, account, wallet, identity, MTCN, or status API action can run while partner review is pending.

blocked.label: Money movement unavailable
blocked.description: Creating, funding, submitting, changing, cancelling, refunding, receiving, or otherwise controlling transfers and payouts remains outside Relay's planned read-only V1 even after partner approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Partner review pending
approvalProfiles.description: Agent actions remain unavailable until Western Union approves Relay's partner integration and engineering implements and validates the exact read-only contract.

runtimeSupport.description: No OpenClaw tools are callable until Western Union approves Relay and Relay implements the contracted read-only Railway broker.
No Hermes tools are callable until Western Union approves Relay and Relay implements the contracted read-only Railway broker.

providerSetup.blocker: Western Union publicly offers full-featured Quick Cash APIs for approved organizations and describes dedicated account-managed onboarding, but its public site does not provide self-service developer credentials, OAuth scopes, a sandbox, a customer authorization lifecycle, or a distributable public API contract. Relay has no signed partner agreement, compliance allocation, approved operations, credentials, representative tenant, or test corridor.
providerSetup.nextAction: An authorized Relay business and compliance owner must contact Western Union's business payments team and obtain the current Quick Cash or other suitable partner API contract, supported jurisdictions and corridors, regulatory and KYC responsibilities, end-user authorization and revocation lifecycle, permitted read-only operations, MTCN and identity-data handling rules, retention terms, rate limits, webhook rules, sandbox tenant, representative test identities, and production onboarding terms. Engineering can then design the smallest read-only corridor, quote, and exact transfer-status V1, implement a fixed-origin Railway broker, and validate authorization, redaction, bounds, rate limits, disconnect, revocation, and post-disconnect denial in staging. Money movement remains excluded.

evidence.supports: Western Union's current business page offers full-featured Quick Cash APIs for mass payments and requires organizations to complete account-managed onboarding before connecting to its platform.

Western Union documents its current consumer send and receive network across online, app, bank-account, cash-pickup, and mobile-wallet delivery methods, including transfer tracking and MTCN requirements.
Western Union's money-transfer terms identify the regulated Western Union entity or licensed partner that provides service in the applicable sending country.

Western Union's agent FAQ describes provider-supplied software, country-dependent eligibility, licensing, regulation, and anti-money-laundering compliance for organizations offering transfer services.
Western Union presents its regulated cross-border money-transfer products for consumers and businesses through digital and physical channels.
